objectives.statement: Identify the municipality's status as the basic local entity and distinguish its elements under the Local Regime Basic Law.
Explain the municipality's territorial element and the rule that each municipality belongs to a single province.
Identify the municipal population register and its relationship to municipal resident status.
Distinguish the general and special municipal organisation rules applicable to local entities.
Identify the mandatory municipal organs present in every municipality.
Apply the population threshold and alternative legal bases for the mandatory Local Government Board.
Explain the Mayor's principal functions as representative, head of government and administration, and convener of municipal bodies.
Identify the Plenary's control and oversight function over the municipal executive.
Distinguish matters reserved to the Plenary from those assigned to the Mayor or Local Government Board.
Explain the composition and delegated-function role of the Local Government Board.
Identify the province as a local entity determined by the grouping of municipalities and as a territorial division for state activity.
Identify the mandatory organs of the provincial council.
Explain the provincial President's representation, direction and convocation powers.
Identify the Plenary of the provincial council's control and oversight competence.
Apply the provincial council's assistance and cooperation duties toward municipalities.
Identify the provincial council's coordination role for municipal services and supra-municipal service provision.
Distinguish provincial organisation from the special organisation rules for island territories.
Explain the role of the provincial council in cooperation with municipalities in economic and technical matters.
Identify the conditions under which a province may provide services beyond the municipal sphere.
Relate municipal and provincial autonomy to the organisation and functions established by the Local Regime Basic Law.
